newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen steady above 116 yen, near peaks vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen steady above 116 yen, near peaks vs mark.

text.p: The dollar was steady above 116 yen and near peaks around 1.6970 marks at midday in Europe, buoyed after French-election results increased expectations of a broad-based start to EMU, analysts said.

"The election results suggest, if repeated next Sunday, that you are likely to get a broader grouping towards EMU (European Monetary Union), which does suggest that the euro will be a weaker currency ," said Jeremy Stretch currency strategist at NatWest Markets.
A softer euro would benefit currencies outside the system such as the dollar and the Swiss franc, said analysts.
At 1005 GMT dollar/mark was trading at 1.6968/78 against 1.6897/02 in late Europe on Monday, though just off peaks around 1.6975 marks touched earlier.
At midday Europe, dollar/yen stood at 116.25 yen, reclaiming its footing after it sank to lows around 115.92 yen earlier.

Analysts said markets were focused on France after an unexpectedly strong showing on Sunday by left-wing parties in the first round of a snap general election called by French President Jacques Chirac. Against most expectations and polls, the opposition left got 44 percent of the votes, when counting the Greens, which has an electoral pact with the Socialists.
But analysts said the dollar was still struggling to find its sense of direction after sinking last week to five-month lows below 112 yen on expectations of higher rates in Japan.

"The market is still trying to work out what the next move in the dollar will be...It is sitting on its hands and waiting to see what the current policy is concerning the dollar in both the U.S. and Japan," said Stretch.
"We are probably going to see a gentle drift higher as the market realises that Japan is not going to move rates, near term, and the U.S. economy still remains pretty firm," said NatWest's Stretch.

Analysts said recent comments from Japanese officials have helped steady dollar/yen. Senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, for instance, told a parliamentary committee meeting on Tuesday that exchange rates are now stable as an accord by the Group of Seven (G7) nations in late April has filtered through markets.

US April consumer confidence and existing home sales due at 1400 GMT will be watched but are not expected to sway the dollar much one way or another. "Near-term influence will be the U.S. data, but it will be of secondary importance to next week's figures," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
